data.gender_notes: Houshiar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Someone who is wise, intelligent, and learned. Derived from the Persian word 'housh' meaning wisdom and 'iar' meaning leader or ruler. The name Houshiar carries the meaning “Wise, Intelligent, Learned” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Persian. Parents who choose Houshiar usually hope their child will grow to embody wise, intelligent, learned and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Houshiar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wise, Intelligent, Learned.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Houshiar total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

historical_references.reference: Houshiar Djevani (1405-1481 CE): Known as the 'Lion of Ghor', Houshiar was a military leader and the last independent ruler of the Ghorid Empire in Afghanistan. He successfully defended his territories against Timurid and Mughal invasions, but was ultimately defeated and killed by the Uzbek commander, Muhammad Shaybani, in 1438.

Houshiar Dergahchi (1572-1632 CE): A Persian poet, Houshiar Dergahchi is best known for his masterpiece, the 'Divan-e Houshiari', which is considered one of the most significant works of Persian literature. He wrote in both Persian and Turkish, and his poetry reflects the social and political turmoil of the Safavid Empire during his time.
